text.p: Germany's Siemens AG was headed for a clear pretax profit rise this year even though the company itself has forecast no improvement, two German business magazine reported.

Manager Magazin, attributing company plans, said pretax profit was seen rising to over four billion marks, thanks to a 300 million mark improvement in medical technology results, firmer semiconductor prices and a smaller than expected loss in the transportation technology unit.

Capital, another magazine, said pretax profit for the year ending September 30 would total 3.5 billion marks -- up from the 1995/96 total of 3.3 billion marks. After-tax profit in the first half was unchanged at 1.08 billion marks.
A Siemens spokesman declined to comment on the reports because the company's nine-month results are due on Monday, but he repeated the forecast for flat earnings.
Siemens shares have risen sharply recently, closing floor trading on Thursday at 118.25 marks, up 15 percent since June 30 and 64 percent from the beginning of the year.

Analysts have said the rise stemmed from expectations that earnings would begin rising again next year as a result of divestments from low-profit businesses, productivity gains and international expansion.
